desc: Jama Masjid is one of the largest mosques in India, located in Old Delhi. Built by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan between 1650 and 1656, it is a masterpiece of Mughal architecture. The mosque has three great gates, four towers, and two 40-meter-high minarets constructed from red sandstone and white marble. Its courtyard can accommodate up to 25,000 worshippers. The mosque stands directly across from the Red Fort on the other side of Chandni Chowk.
fact: It was built by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan between 1650 and 1656 · Its courtyard can accommodate up to 25,000 worshippers · It has two 40-meter-high minarets of red sandstone and white marble · It stands across from the Red Fort in Old Delhi

desc: Mecca Masjid is one of the largest mosques in India, located in Hyderabad near the Charminar. Construction was started in 1614 by Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah and completed by Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb in 1693. The mosque can accommodate up to 20,000 worshippers. Its name derives from the bricks brought from Mecca used in its construction. The mosque's hall features impressive granite pillars and arches, with the main ceiling decorated with exquisite calligraphy.
fact: It was started in 1614 by Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah and completed in 1693 · It can accommodate up to 20,000 worshippers · Bricks brought from Mecca were used in its construction · It is located near the Charminar in Hyderabad

desc: Taj-ul-Masajid, meaning 'Crown of Mosques,' is the largest mosque in India, located in Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh. Its construction was started by Nawab Shah Jahan Begum of Bhopal in 1871 and completed in 1971 after a century-long hiatus. The mosque features a stunning pink facade, two main minarets, and three massive domes. The main prayer hall has 27 arches with intricate carvings. The mosque can accommodate over 175,000 worshippers during Eid prayers.
fact: It is the largest mosque in India, accommodating over 175,000 worshippers · Construction started in 1871 and was completed exactly a century later in 1971 · It features a pink facade, two minarets, and three massive domes · It was built by Nawab Shah Jahan Begum of Bhopal

desc: Haji Ali Dargah is a mosque and dargah (shrine) located on an islet off the coast of Worli in Mumbai. Built in 1431 in memory of the Muslim saint Pir Haji Ali Shah Bukhari, the structure is accessible only during low tide via a narrow causeway. The shrine features Indo-Islamic architecture with white domes and minarets. It is one of Mumbai's most recognizable landmarks and attracts thousands of devotees from all religions, especially on Thursdays and Fridays.
fact: It is located on an islet off the coast of Worli in Mumbai, accessible only at low tide · It was built in 1431 in memory of Muslim saint Pir Haji Ali Shah Bukhari · It features Indo-Islamic architecture with white domes · It is one of Mumbai's most recognizable landmarks

desc: Cheraman Juma Mosque is the first mosque in India, built in 629 AD by Malik Deenar, an Arab missionary, at the request of Cheraman Perumal, the Chera king who embraced Islam. Located in Methala, Kodungallur, Kerala, it was built in the Kerala architectural style with a traditional mosque structure and a pond. The mosque houses an ancient oil lamp that has been burning for over 1,000 years. It stands as a symbol of religious harmony and the early spread of Islam in South Asia.
fact: It is the first mosque in India, built in 629 AD · It was built by Malik Deenar at the request of Cheraman Perumal, the Chera king · It was built in Kerala architectural style with a traditional mosque structure · The mosque houses an oil lamp that has been burning for over 1,000 years

desc: Jama Masjid of Mumbai is the largest mosque in Mumbai, located in the Kalbadevi area near Crawford Market. Built in 1802 by the Konkani Muslim community, the mosque features an impressive pink-and-cream facade with intricate Mughal-style arches and domes. The mosque underwent major renovations in the late 20th century. It serves as the primary mosque for Mumbai's Muslim community and is a prominent landmark in the city's historic district.
fact: It is the largest mosque in Mumbai, built in 1802 · It features a pink-and-cream facade with Mughal-style arches and domes · It was built by the Konkani Muslim community · It is located in the Kalbadevi area near Crawford Market

desc: Nagina Masjid, meaning 'Gem Mosque,' is a historic mosque located within the Agra Fort, built by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan between 1631 and 1640. It is constructed entirely of white marble, earning its name for its gem-like appearance. The mosque features three domes and a courtyard with elegant arcades. It was used as a private place of worship by the emperor and the royal ladies of the Mughal court. The mosque stands near the Machchhi Bhawan in the fort complex.
fact: It is located within the Agra Fort, built by Shah Jahan between 1631-1640 · It is constructed entirely of white marble · It was used as a private mosque by the Mughal royal family · The name means 'Gem Mosque' for its jewel-like white marble appearance

desc: Moti Masjid, meaning 'Pearl Mosque,' is a white marble mosque located inside the Agra Fort, built by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan between 1646 and 1653. The mosque earned its name for the pearly sheen of its white marble construction. It features three bulbous domes and a simple yet elegant design. The prayer hall has seven arches with the central arch being the tallest. Unlike many Mughal structures, the Moti Masjid lacks minarets and is known for its purity of form.
fact: It means 'Pearl Mosque' for the pearly sheen of its white marble · It was built by Shah Jahan between 1646-1653 inside the Agra Fort · It features three bulbous domes and seven arches in the prayer hall · The mosque lacks minarets and is known for its pure, simple design

desc: Sidi Bashir Mosque is a historic mosque in Ahmedabad, Gujarat, famous for its two towering minarets known as the 'Shaking Minarets' or Jhulta Minars. Built in 1452 by Sidi Bashir, a slave of Sultan Ahmed Shah, the minarets are a marvel of engineering — when one minaret is shaken, the other vibrates in response. The minarets feature intricate Islamic carvings and balconies. The mosque was part of the Ahmedabad UNESCO World Heritage City designation.
fact: It is famous for its 'Shaking Minarets' — when one is shaken, the other vibrates · Built in 1452 by Sidi Bashir, a slave of Sultan Ahmed Shah · The minarets feature intricate Islamic carvings and balconies · The mosque is in Ahmedabad, a UNESCO World Heritage City

desc: Tipu Sultan Mosque is a historic mosque located in the Esplanade area of Kolkata, West Bengal. Built in 1832 by Prince Ghulam Mohammed, the youngest son of Tipu Sultan, the mosque is an excellent example of Indo-Islamic architecture. It features two majestic minarets, large domes, and intricate Islamic calligraphy. The mosque has a large prayer hall with arched windows and is built in red sandstone with white marble detailing. It remains an active place of worship and a heritage landmark in central Kolkata.
fact: It was built in 1832 by Prince Ghulam Mohammed, the youngest son of Tipu Sultan · It features two minarets, large domes, and intricate calligraphy · It is built in red sandstone with white marble detailing · It is a heritage landmark in the Esplanade area of Kolkata
